parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: HAZOP node V-001. Design intent (inferred): maintain a controlled separator liquid level so liquid leaves via the LV and gas leaves liquid-free to gas treatment. Guideword/deviation: MORE LEVEL. Causes (P2): LV failing closed; spurious SDV closure (interpreted as a liquid-outlet SDV). Consequence (P3): flooding, liquid carryover into the gas-treatment line, unit shutdown, production loss. Safeguards (CASE-03, P1): LAH-102 and LAHH-103, both closing SDV-30010. Ex ante basis: there is no diagnostic trend, verified initiating fault or occurrence (P3), so only a base-rate judgment is possible. Using generic order-of-magnitude reliability ranges (not plant data), a high-level demand from the two listed causes is judged roughly 1-5% likely in 30 operating days. The target event further requires the high-level protection to fail or act too late. Both safeguards share one final element (SDV-30010) and their sensing/logic independence is unstated, so their combined probability of failure on demand is judged ~0.02-0.1 rather than the product of two independent layers. Estimate ~0.3%, set toward the upper part of the ~0.02-0.5% product range to reflect unverified independence, testing and response time. Predictability 10%: the scenario class was foreseen with causes and safeguards, but no precursor allowed its occurrence within the window to be predicted. Assessor's own qualitative risk (source rating withheld): low likelihood x moderate operational/asset severity, giving medium-low priority, tolerable subject to verification of safeguard integrity. Negligence: none attributable; the hazard was identified, safeguards were specified, and no ignored warning or known fault is evidenced pre-event. Recommendations: verify that LAH-102 and LAHH-103 are independent of each other and of the LV control loop; perform a LOPA/SIL review of whether the shared SDV-30010 merits one or two layers of credit; confirm SDV-30010 proof-test status and closure time versus time-to-overflow; review causes of spurious SDV trips; if a gap remains, consider a diverse final element or downstream liquid detection.
